message.content:
**Quick ways to see if VS Code is running on Windows** | Method | What to do | What you’ll see | |--------|------------|-----------------| | **Task Manager** | Press `Ctrl + Shift + Esc` (or right‑click the taskbar → “Task Manager”). | In the **Processes** tab look for **Code.exe** (or “Visual Studio Code”). If it’s there, VS Code is running. | | **Command Prompt** | Open a normal CMD window (`Win + R`, type `cmd`, hit Enter). Run:
`tasklist | findstr /i Code.exe` | If VS Code is running you’ll get a line like `Code.exe …`. If nothing appears, it’s not running. | | **PowerShell** | Open PowerShell (`Win + X` → “Windows PowerShell” or “Windows Terminal”). Run:
`Get-Process -Name Code -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` | If the process exists you’ll see its details; otherwise nothing will be returned. | --- ### If you want to **stop** it ```cmd taskkill /IM Code.exe /F ``` > This force‑kills the VS Code process. Use it only if you’re sure you want to close it. --- ### Quick script you can paste into a `.bat` file ```bat @echo off tasklist | findstr /i Code.exe >nul if %errorlevel%==0 ( echo VS Code is running. ) else ( echo VS Code is NOT running. ) pause ``` Save as `check_vscode.bat`, double‑click it, and it will tell you whether VS Code is active. --- **Tip:** If you’re using VS Code’s built‑in terminal, you can also run the same `tasklist | findstr /i Code.exe` command directly there. It will give you the same result.
